project.name: libspectre
project.commit_note: The exact staged vulnerable source inspected for Stage 02 is the ARVO workspace checkout at `945d39259c0ca1dfd6c594a9d3ed971152313190`, whose `libspectre/ps.c` line map matches the statements cited below. Sample metadata separately records `dd7168828cf07971adc8c24bab0f3b6e3d28e0c9` / `48735999ca27fca8f154aa15c078c4576ab64ae5` as the issue's vulnerable/fixed commits.

classification.classification_note: Sample metadata labels the issue `unclassified`, but the staged source, patch, and Stage 01 MemorySanitizer report show an unchecked short read that leaves stack bytes in `DOSEPS doseps.id` uninitialized before they are compared.

bug_description.original: A vulnerability allows uninitialized memory to be read when processing malformed documents.
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` in `ps_read_doseps()` while libspectre processed the exact staged malformed document `poc`, which is a single byte `0xC5`. `document_load()` enters `psscan()`, which stack-allocates `DOSEPS doseps` and immediately calls `ps_read_doseps(fd, &doseps)` to probe for a DOS EPS header. In the vulnerable source, `ps_read_doseps()` executes `fread(doseps->id, 1, 4, FD_FILE)` but does not check how many bytes were actually read before comparing `doseps->id[0..3]` against the DOS EPS magic `c5 d0 d3 c6`. For the one-byte witness, `fread` initializes only `doseps->id[0] = 0xc5`; `doseps->id[1..3]` remain uninitialized stack bytes from `psscan`. Because the first conjunct `doseps->id[0]==0xc5` succeeds, evaluation reaches the next comparison `doseps->id[1]==0xd0`, which reads an untouched stack byte; MemorySanitizer reports the enclosing multi-line condition at `libspectre/ps.c:2215`. The patch fixes the exact obligation by saving the `fread` return value and requiring `read == 4` before any `doseps->id[]` comparison.

source.description: First project-code statement that consumes the attacker-controlled document bytes for the vulnerable DOS EPS header probe.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` file is exactly one byte `0xC5`. This `fread(..., 4, ...)` can therefore initialize only `doseps->id[0] = 0xC5` and returns a short count, leaving `doseps->id[1]` and the remaining unread positions untouched.

tainted_value_origin.description: The uninitialized byte later consumed at the witnessed sink is `doseps.id[1]` inside this stack object. It starts indeterminate here, and the short read in `ps_read_doseps()` initializes only `doseps.id[0]` before the next comparison executes.
tainted_value_origin.note: The saved MemorySanitizer report attributes the poisoned value to the allocation of `doseps` in `psscan` and reports line 372 in the instrumented build; the exact staged declaration in the current source snapshot is line 398.

sink.description: Sanitizer-reported location for the multi-line DOS EPS magic predicate. On the exact one-byte witness, the true first conjunct forces evaluation of the next comparison `doseps->id[1]==0xd0`, which reads an uninitialized stack byte.
sink.note: The staged `sanitizer_trace.txt` reports `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` at `libspectre/ps.c:2215:5` for this multi-line `if` and attributes the origin to stack allocation of `doseps` in `psscan`.

root_cause.description: Missing full-read guard: the DOS EPS magic predicate dereferences `doseps->id[]` without first checking that `fread` initialized all 4 bytes.
root_cause.note: The patch captures `const size_t read = fread(...)` and adds `read == 4` as the leftmost conjunct. In the vulnerable code, the return value is discarded, so a short read still reaches the next byte comparison on partially initialized stack storage.

parser_admitted.description: The attacker-controlled stream is admitted into libspectre's PostScript scanner here; the witnessed path then reaches `psscan()` and its DOS EPS probe.
parser_admitted.condition: `file` is non-NULL for the staged harness run, so `document_load()` does not return early and enters `psscan()`.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness wraps the exact one-byte witness `0xC5` in an in-memory `FILE *` and calls libspectre's stream loader.
libspectre dispatches the stream into `psscan()` for PostScript parsing.
The scanner stack-allocates `DOSEPS doseps` and calls `ps_read_doseps(fd, &doseps)` to test whether the stream starts with a DOS EPS header.

A 4-byte header read from the 1-byte witness initializes only `doseps->id[0]`; without a `read == 4` guard, the DOS EPS magic check reaches the next comparison `doseps->id[1]==0xd0`, and MSAN reports the enclosing `if` at line 2215.

fine_trace.note: Allocates the `DOSEPS` stack object without initialization. Until later writes occur, all four `doseps.id` bytes are indeterminate; MSAN names this stack object as the origin.

Source. `psscan()` passed step 1's stack object by address into `ps_read_doseps()`, and this read copies attacker-controlled header bytes into `doseps->id`. For the exact one-byte witness `0xC5`, only `doseps->id[0]` becomes defined; `doseps->id[1..3]` remain uninitialized stack bytes.

Missing guard. The predicate uses `doseps->id[]` immediately after step 2 and never checks whether all 4 bytes were read. The patch adds `read == 4` ahead of these comparisons. On the exact witness, the first conjunct `doseps->id[0]==0xc5` is true, so evaluation reaches the next magic-byte test `doseps->id[1]==0xd0` instead of stopping at the initialized prefix.

Sink. Step 2 left `doseps->id[1]` untouched, and step 3's missing `read == 4` guard allows the next conjunct `doseps->id[1]==0xd0` to execute once `doseps->id[0]==0xc5` succeeds. Stage 01's saved MSAN run reports `use-of-uninitialized-value` at `libspectre/ps.c:2215:5`, the reported location of this multi-line `if`.

allocation_context.note: The saved trace says the uninitialized value was created by allocation of `doseps` in the stack frame of `psscan` at line 372; the exact staged declaration in the inspected source snapshot is `DOSEPS doseps;` at line 398.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Yes. The saved MSan origin names `doseps` in the `psscan` stack frame; fine-trace step 1 is the exact staged `DOSEPS doseps;` declaration, and step 3 is the adjacent missing `read == 4` obligation that lets those same bytes reach the sink.
cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch saves the `fread` result and requires `read == 4` before any `doseps->id[]` comparison, which directly blocks the witnessed one-byte path before `doseps->id[1]` is tested.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's authoritative vulnerable run executes `/out/spectre_read_fuzzer /tmp/poc` and reproduces `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` in `ps_read_doseps`.

format.name: Raw byte stream treated by libspectre as a PostScript/DOS-EPS candidate document
format.contract: The verified trigger is the exact staged one-byte witness `c5`. When `spectre_read_fuzzer` loads this stream, `ps_read_doseps()` asks `fread` for 4 header bytes, receives only that one byte, and then evaluates the DOS EPS magic-byte `&&` chain without first requiring a full 4-byte read. The first comparison succeeds because the witness byte is `0xC5`, so evaluation reaches the next comparison `doseps->id[1]==0xd0`, which reads an uninitialized stack byte; MemorySanitizer reports `use-of-uninitialized-value` at the enclosing multi-line condition in `libspectre/ps.c:2215`. The staged artifacts do not prove which other short prefixes would follow the same path, so the contract should not be generalized beyond this exact witness.
